claimBeforeHumanConfirmation.statement: On this deterministic 1-D synthetic quadratic fixture (loss=(x-3)^2, initial points x0 = -1, 0, 1, target 3, ten full-batch gradient steps, Node/CPU), raising the learning rate from 0.1 to 0.2 while varying nothing else lowered final_loss for each of the three fixed initial points (0.1844674407370954 -> 0.0005849853504100812; 0.10376293541461637 -> 0.0003290542596056707; 0.04611686018427375 -> 0.0001462463376025203) and lowered mean final_loss from 0.11144907877866184 (lr=0.1) to 0.00035342864920609067 (lr=0.2), a delta of -0.11109565012945574 and ratio 0.003171211938934021 as computed by the reproducible QA comparison script (analyticRatio 0.0031712119389339837).
claimBeforeHumanConfirmation.limitations: Scope is exactly this synthetic convex quadratic, exactly three deterministic initial points, and exactly ten gradient steps at two learning rates (0.1 and 0.2). The three "seeds" differ only in deterministic initialization, so this is not a sample of independent replicates: no statistical independence, variance, uncertainty or significance inference follows. The result is a paired comparison of two fixed configurations, not a learning-rate sweep, and it does not establish an optimality claim or any ordering for other learning rates, other objectives, other step budgets, stochastic/minibatch training, or other dimensions and environments. All numbers are quoted from tool-produced artifacts; no untested stability or step-size regime was examined and none is implied.
